ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the power supply is marked with electromotive force E and internal resistance r, and there is switch S at the bottom; an ammeter A is connected in series at the lower left side, and there is resistor R2 at the lower right side; a sliding rheostat is connected between the middle left and right nodes, with the right end marked b and the left side marked a, and slider P is connected by a wire to the left node; in the middle there is also voltmeter V connected in parallel between the left and right nodes; the upper branch goes from the left node through R1 and capacitor C to the right node. Reasoning: After S is closed and direct current is stable, the upper branch where capacitor C is located is equivalent to an open circuit, so this branch has no sustained current; the current in the ideal voltmeter branch can be ignored. Thus the main loop is equivalent to power supply E, internal resistance r, R2, and the actually connected part of the sliding rheostat connected in series. Since in the figure slider P is connected to the left node, the part from a to P of the sliding rheostat is bypassed, and what is actually connected is the section from P to b. When P moves from the position shown in the figure toward end a, the length from P to b becomes longer, so R_Pb increases, and the total resistance r+R2+R_Pb increases. When E is unchanged, the loop current I=E/(r+R2+R_Pb) decreases. Final answer: The ammeter reading I becomes smaller.
